title: Prefetching Audit Canary and Regression Certifier
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Automated batching/prefetch/caching recommendations reduce cost but risk subtle quality regressions for long-form or multi-turn flows. Current autotune applies knob changes with simple smoke checks; we need a stronger certifier that uses progressive canaries and explainable regression signals tied to the optimizer so we can safely apply or rollback changes automatically.

Goal: Build a Prefetching Audit Canary and Regression Certifier (PAC-RC) that: 1) verifies proposed batching/prefetch/cache configurations against a stratified golden corpus, 2) produces explainable regression scores (semantic drift, token-behavior deltas, hallucination indicators), 3) runs progressive canaries (shadow -> small canary -> ramp) and 4) integrates with the existing autoscale/autotune pipeline to block auto-apply if thresholds are exceeded and enable safe rollback automation when needed.
acceptance_criteria: A1: PAC-RC runs in CI for any config change and produces a per-config report within 45 minutes for the standard gold corpus (~2.5K prompts)
A2: Regression signal types implemented: embedding similarity delta, response length distribution shift, top-token probability shift, named-entity retention recall
A3: Canary rollout gates integrated into autotune: shadow-only, 1% production traffic, 10% ramp; each gate must pass numeric thresholds before progressing
A4: Automatic rollback trigger implemented: if canary fails at any stage according to rules, the change is reverted and incident ticket auto-created with diagnostics
A5: Human-in-the-loop review step for any config that marginally fails (threshold window), with a UI link to sample diffs and aggregated metrics
eval_suite: Stratified eval harness composed of: (a) core gold prompts (700 conversational anchors), (b) long-form synthesis set (600 examples), (c) slot-filling/regression set (500 prompts), (d) adversarial style perturbations (700 prompts). The harness computes per-batch deltas and bootstrapped confidence intervals for all metrics.
golden_prompts: conversational-anchor-v1 (700 prompts): typical multi-turn consumer assistant queries
longform-essays-v2 (600 prompts): open-ended generation with target length distributions
slotfill-retention-v1 (500 prompts): entity-heavy prompts where recall matters
perturb-adversarial-v1 (700 prompts): paraphrase/noise to surface brittle behavior
thresholds: Embedding similarity: mean cosine drop > 0.04 (vs baseline) and bootstrap p-value < 0.01 => fail
Top-token shift: KL divergence > 0.15 on next-token distribution => suspect
Length distribution: KL divergence > 0.12 for any major intent cohort => suspect
NER recall drop: > 6% absolute decrease => fail
Hallucination indicator (entity hallucination rate): increase > 3% => fail
Marginal window: signals between suspect and fail trigger human review (HITL)
rollout_plan: 1) CI gate: run PAC-RC for every autotune candidate; block PR if fail. 2) Shadow apply: metric logging & manual review for 48 hours. 3) Micro canary: 1% production traffic for 6 hours with automated check; if pass, ramp to 10% for 24 hours. 4) Full apply: after 3 successful rollouts in separate clusters, mark as default. All stages record reports and diffs to the rollout dashboard.
rollback_plan:
- Automatic: immediate rollback if a 'fail' threshold is reached during canary with rollback executed by autotune orchestrator and change tagged as 'reverted by PAC-RC'.
- Semi-automatic: if marginal window hit, pause ramp and notify SRE/ML owner to approve either continue or rollback within 2 hours.
- Postmortem: auto-create incident with summary, link to sample inputs, model outputs, embeddings, and the failing metric slices.
monitoring_checks: Per-route token-cost delta (alert if >5% increase post-change)
End-to-end latency P95 (alert if regression >10ms and impact on SLO)
Per-customer quality delta: cohorted checks for top 10 customers
Data drift: input distribution shift detector for prompt length and language (alert if KL > 0.08)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: conservative thresholds slow rollout velocity but reduce user-facing regressions; expensive CI runs increase cost and time (we mitigate with stratified cores and prioritized early exits). We prefer explainable signals (embedding deltas + NER recall) over blackbox pass/fail models to make HITL reviews productive. Future: incorporate user-telemetry signals (support tickets/negative feedback) into the certifier once privacy workaround is approved.
